easy.def: A small piece that you pull.
examples: Pull the tab.
The tab on the can opens it.
The tab is small.

more.def: A small flap or piece that sticks out so you can pull or press it.
examples: Pull the tab to open the can.
The file folder has a tab with my name.
I clicked the tab on the screen.

easy.def: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.
examples: We eat at the table.
The book is on the table.
Set the table.

more.def: A piece of furniture with a flat top held up by legs.
examples: We sat around the table for dinner.
The cat jumped onto the table.
She set the table with plates and forks.

easy.def: Facts in neat rows.
examples: The table shows the scores.
Look at the table.
Fill in the table.

more.def: Information arranged in rows and columns so it is easy to read.
examples: The table shows how many books each class read.
I made a table of the daily temperatures.
Use the table to find the answer.

easy.def: A flat computer you touch with your finger.
examples: I play games on a tablet.
The tablet is on the desk.
She read a book on the tablet.

more.def: A flat, light computer with a touch screen that you can carry around and use without a keyboard.
examples: I read a story on my tablet in the car.
The teacher handed out tablets for the class project.
He drew a picture on the tablet with his finger.

easy.def: A small, hard piece of medicine.
examples: She took a tablet.
The tablet is small.
Mom gave me a tablet for my cold.

more.def: A small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow.
examples: The doctor told him to take one tablet with water every morning.
The tablet dissolves in water and fizzes.
Take a tablet only when a grown-up gives it to you.

easy.def: To take on a hard job.
examples: I tackle my homework.
She tackled the puzzle.
He tackled the problem.

more.def: To begin to deal with a hard task, or to grab and stop a football player.
examples: I tackled the hard math problem.
She tackled the puzzle after lunch.
The player tackled the runner.

easy.def: The tools for fishing.
examples: The fishing tackle is in the box.
He bought new tackle.
The tackle is in the boat.

more.def: The equipment that is used for fishing.
examples: The fishing tackle is kept in the box.
Dad bought new tackle for the trip.
The tackle was stored in the boat.

easy.def: A folded tortilla with food inside.
examples: I ate a taco.
The taco has cheese.
We had tacos for dinner.

more.def: A folded corn or flour tortilla filled with meat, cheese and vegetables.
examples: I ate a taco with cheese and lettuce.
Tacos are fun to make at home.
He dropped a bit of his taco on the plate.

easy.def: The plans you use to win a game or reach a goal.
examples: Our tactics helped us win.
The coach talked about tactics.
We used a new tactic.

more.def: The clever plans or steps used to try to win a game or reach a goal.
examples: The coach taught us new tactics for stopping the other team.
Chess players study tactics to plan their moves ahead.
Her tactics for the spelling bee included practicing every night.

easy.def: A very small amount.
examples: Add just a tad of salt.
I am a tad tired.
He ate a tad of cake.

more.def: A tiny bit; a very small amount.
examples: Add a tad more water to the soup and stir it.
She was a tad nervous before she went on stage.
The shirt is a tad too small for me now.

easy.def: A small label.
examples: The tag shows the price.
My coat has a name tag.
The dog has a tag.

more.def: A small piece of paper or cloth that has information on it, fixed to something.
examples: The tag on the shirt shows the size.
My dog wears a tag with its name on it.
Dad checked the price tag.

easy.def: A running game where one person chases the others.
examples: We play tag at recess.
I am it in tag.
The kids played tag.

more.def: A game in which one player chases the others and tries to touch them.
examples: We play tag on the playground.
She was it in the game of tag.
The kids ran in circles during tag.

easy.def: The part at the back of an animal.
examples: The dog wags its tail.
A cat has a long tail.
The monkey's tail curled.

more.def: The long part that sticks out from the back of an animal.
examples: The dog wagged its tail.
A fox has a bushy tail.
The monkey wrapped its tail around the branch.

easy.def: The back part of something.
examples: The tail of the plane.
The tail of the kite.
The tail of the comet.

more.def: The back end of something, such as a plane or a kite.
examples: The kite's long tail fluttered.
The tail of the plane was painted red.
The comet's bright tail stretched across the sky.

easy.def: A person who makes or fixes clothes.
examples: The tailor fixed my pants.
A tailor sews.
The tailor measured me.

more.def: A person whose job is to make or fix clothes so that they fit.
examples: The tailor shortened my pants.
A tailor measured the man for a suit.
The tailor sewed a button on my coat.

easy.def: To get hold of something and bring it along.
examples: Take your hat.
I took my book to school.
She takes the dog out.

more.def: To carry something with you, or to grab or accept something.
examples: Please take an umbrella because it might rain.
He took a cookie from the plate on the counter.
I will take you to the museum on Saturday.

easy.def: A story.
examples: I read a tale about a fox.
The tale was funny.
Grandpa told a tale.

more.def: A story, especially one that is made up or told aloud.
examples: Grandpa told us a tale about a clever fox.
The fairy tale ended happily.
She wrote a tale about a dragon.

easy.def: Something you are very good at.
examples: She has a talent for singing.
Drawing is his talent.
We will have a talent show.

more.def: A natural ability to do something well.
examples: His talent for drawing was clear even when he was little.
She showed her talent at the piano concert.
He has a real talent for making people laugh.

easy.def: Having a special skill.
examples: She is a talented singer.
The talented boy draws well.
A talented player.

more.def: Having a natural skill or ability to do something well.
examples: The talented young pianist played for hours.
The talented boy draws amazing pictures.
The team has many talented players.

easy.def: To say words to someone.
examples: I talk to my friend.
She talks a lot.
We talked on the phone.

more.def: To speak with someone and share thoughts or ideas.
examples: The two neighbors talked over the fence about the garden.
Please do not talk while the teacher is reading.
He talked to the class about his trip to Mexico.

easy.def: High from bottom to top.
examples: The tree is tall.
My dad is tall.
A tall building.

more.def: Having a great height from bottom to top.
examples: The giraffe is the tallest animal.
A tall tree grows by the gate.
She is taller than her brother.

easy.def: A count of how many there are.
examples: Keep a tally of the points.
The tally was ten.
I made a tally.

more.def: A count or record of numbers or scores.
examples: Keep a tally of the points as we play.
The tally of votes showed that the red team won.
I made a tally of the birds I saw at the feeder.

easy.def: To count up a number.
examples: I tally the votes.
We tallied the points.
She tallied the cookies.

more.def: To count up a total of something.
examples: I tally the votes at the end of the day.
We tallied the points after the last game.
She tallied the cookies that were sold at the bake sale.

easy.def: Not wild; used to being around people.
examples: The bird is tame.
A tame rabbit.
The tame fox ate from my hand.

more.def: Not afraid of people and not wild, or trained to live with people.
examples: The tame bird landed on my shoulder.
We have a tame rabbit that loves to be petted.
The deer was so tame that it ate from her hand.

easy.def: To make a wild animal gentle and used to people.
examples: He tries to tame the horse.
She tamed the bird.
They tamed the wolf.

more.def: To train a wild animal so that it is gentle and not afraid of people.
examples: He worked all summer to tame the wild horse.
She tamed a young bird by feeding it every day.
The farmer tamed the fox cub that he found.

related.def: A person who trains wild animals.

easy.def: A light brown color.
examples: The dog is tan.
She wore a tan coat.
The sand is tan.

more.def: Having a light yellowish-brown color.
examples: The puppy had a tan coat.
She wore tan shoes.
The desert sand was tan.

easy.def: Brown skin from being in the sun.
examples: I got a tan.
The tan faded.
He has a tan.

more.def: The browning of skin from spending time in the sun.
examples: She got a tan at the beach.
His tan faded by winter.
The sun gave us a tan.

easy.def: A messy bunch of things twisted together.
examples: My hair is in a tangle.
The string is a tangle.
A tangle of wires.

more.def: A messy mass of things twisted together.
examples: My hair is in a big tangle.
The kite string was a tangle of knots.
A tangle of vines covered the old fence.

easy.def: To twist together in a messy way.
examples: The strings tangled.
My hair tangles.
The fishing line tangled.

more.def: To twist things together so they are hard to pull apart.
examples: The kite strings tangled in the wind.
My hair tangles when I run fast.
The fishing line tangled around the branch.

easy.def: A dance from Argentina.
examples: They danced the tango.
The tango is slow.
I saw a tango.

more.def: A dramatic, graceful dance for two people that began in Argentina.
examples: They danced the tango at the party.
The tango music was slow and dramatic.
I watched a tango show.

easy.def: A big container for liquid or gas.
examples: The water tank is full.
The gas tank is empty.
The fish tank.

more.def: A large container that holds liquid or gas.
examples: The gas tank was nearly empty.
A water tank sits on top of the building.
The fish swam in the big tank.

easy.def: A heavy military vehicle.
examples: The tank has a big gun.
A tank rolled by.
A tank moves on tracks.

more.def: A heavy military vehicle with a large gun that moves on metal tracks.
examples: A tank rolled down the road.
The museum has an old war tank.
Soldiers rode in the tank.

easy.def: To hit lightly.
examples: Tap me on the shoulder.
She tapped on the door.
I tap my foot.

more.def: To touch or hit something lightly, again and again.
examples: He tapped on the window to get our attention.
She tapped her foot to the music.
The woodpecker tapped on the tree.

easy.def: A thing that you turn to let water out.
examples: Turn the tap off.
The tap is dripping.
Water came out of the tap.

more.def: A device that you turn or press to make water or other liquid flow out of a pipe.
examples: She turned off the tap after washing her hands.
The tap in the kitchen dripped all night.
He filled the glass from the tap.

easy.def: A sticky strip to hold things.
examples: Use tape to fix the paper.
The tape is sticky.
I need tape.

more.def: A thin, sticky strip used to stick things together.
examples: She used tape to hang the poster.
Dad wrapped tape around the box.
The tape ran out before I finished.

easy.def: To stick something with a sticky strip.
examples: Tape the picture to the wall.
She taped the box.
He taped the paper.

more.def: To fasten something using a sticky strip.
examples: Tape the poster to the wall.
She taped the box shut.
He taped the map to the window.

easy.def: Thick, black, sticky stuff used to make roads.
examples: The road is made of tar.
Tar is sticky.
I stepped in tar.

more.def: A thick, black, sticky substance made from coal or wood that is used to cover roads and roofs.
examples: Workers poured hot tar on the road.
The tar was black and sticky on my shoe.
Tar helps keep rain out of the roof.

easy.def: A thing you aim at.
examples: He hit the target.
The arrow hit the target.
The target is round.

more.def: An object or mark that you try to hit.
examples: She aimed the ball at the target.
The arrow hit the center of the target.
Players threw bean bags at the target.

easy.def: A goal you want to reach.
examples: Our target is ten books.
Her target was a perfect score.
We met our target.

more.def: A goal that you are trying to reach.
examples: Our class has a target of reading fifty books.
She set a target of running a mile.
The team met its target.

easy.def: A small pie that has fruit or jam in it.
examples: I ate a tart.
The tart is sweet.
A cherry tart.

more.def: A small, open pie filled with fruit, jam or custard.
examples: I ate a strawberry tart for dessert.
Grandma baked a cherry tart.
A tart with jam on top sat in the bakery window.

easy.def: Sharp and sour in taste.
examples: The lemon is tart.
The apple tastes tart.
A tart berry.

more.def: Having a sharp, sour taste.
examples: The lemon juice tasted tart.
A tart green apple makes a good pie.
The berries were tart without sugar.

easy.def: A job to do.
examples: My task is to feed the cat.
The task is hard.
I finished the task.

more.def: A piece of work that has to be done.
examples: My task is to set the table.
Cleaning the garage was a big task.
The teacher gave us a reading task.

easy.def: The way food feels on your tongue.
examples: I like the taste of honey.
The taste is sweet.
What a sour taste!

more.def: The flavor that something has when you put it in your mouth.
examples: I love the sweet taste of ripe peaches.
Lemons have a sour taste.
The soup had a salty taste.

easy.def: To know the flavor of food.
examples: I taste the soup.
Taste the cake.
The soup tastes good.

more.def: To notice the flavor of something in your mouth.
examples: Taste the soup and tell me if it needs salt.
The bread tastes like honey.
I can taste lemon in the tea.

related.def: A feeling of not liking something.
A person who tastes food or drink to test it.

easy.def: Good to eat.
examples: The soup is tasty.
This is a tasty apple.
Dad made a tasty lunch.

more.def: Having a pleasant flavor.
examples: Grandpa makes a tasty vegetable stew.
The market sells tasty fresh bread.
Add some herbs to make the sauce more tasty.

easy.def: Torn and old.
examples: The flag is tattered.
A tattered shirt.
The book is tattered.

more.def: Old and torn in many places.
examples: The old flag was tattered.
He wore a tattered shirt.
The much-loved book was tattered.

easy.def: A picture on skin that does not wash off.
examples: He has a tattoo on his arm.
The tattoo is a bird.
She has a small tattoo.

more.def: A picture or design that is put into the skin with ink and stays there forever.
examples: The sailor had a tattoo of an anchor on his arm.
She got a tattoo of a rose on her shoulder.
The tattoo will never wash off.

easy.def: Stretched tight.
examples: The rope is taut.
The string was taut.
A taut sail.

more.def: Pulled tight so that it is not loose.
examples: The rope was taut as we pulled the boat.
The string on the kite was taut in the wind.
A taut wire held up the tent.

easy.def: Money that people pay to the government.
examples: We pay a tax when we buy things.
Taxes pay for roads.
Taxes help build schools.

more.def: Money that people and businesses pay to the government to pay for things like roads and schools.
examples: Taxes pay for roads, parks and schools.
The tax on a toy makes it cost a little more.
Families pay taxes every year.

easy.def: A car with a driver that you pay to take you places.
examples: We took a taxi to the airport.
The taxi is yellow.
The taxi stopped for us.

more.def: A car with a driver that takes people where they want to go for money.
examples: We hailed a taxi in the rain.
The taxi driver knew the quickest way to the station.
A taxi took us from the hotel to the train station.
